name: Question 12
problem: Find the Cartesian equation of the hyperbola $x=\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{5}\operatorname{tan}⁡t.$
worked_solution:
To find the Cartesian equation of the hyperbola, we need to eliminate the parameter $t.$ We can do this using the secant-tangent identity.

- Isolating the $\operatorname{sec}⁡t$ term in the $x$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sec}⁡t \\ \frac{x}{\sqrt{3}} & =\operatorname{sec}⁡t \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}} & ={sec}^{2}⁡t \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{3} & ={sec}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

- Isolating the $\operatorname{tan}⁡t$ term in the $y$-equation and squaring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt{5}\operatorname{tan}⁡t \\ \frac{y}{\sqrt{5}} & =\operatorname{tan}⁡t \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{(\sqrt{5})^{2}} & ={tan}^{2}⁡t \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{5} & ={tan}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the two equations into the identity ${tan}^{2}⁡t+1={sec}^{2}⁡t$ and rearranging, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡t+1 & ={sec}^{2}⁡t \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{5}+1 & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{3} \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{5} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Find the Cartesian equation of the hyperbola x=3sec⁡t,y=5tan⁡t.

a
y23−x25=1
b
x25−y23=1
c
x23−y25=1
d
y25−x23=1
e
x29−y225=1
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To find the Cartesian equation of the hyperbola, we need to eliminate the parameter t. We can do this using the secant-tangent identity.

  • Isolating the sec⁡t term in the x-equation and squaring, we get x=3sec⁡tx3=sec⁡tx2(3)2=sec2⁡tx23=sec2⁡t.

  • Isolating the tan⁡t term in the y-equation and squaring, we get y=5tan⁡ty5=tan⁡ty2(5)2=tan2⁡ty25=tan2⁡t.

Substituting the two equations into the identity tan2⁡t+1=sec2⁡t and rearranging, we get

tan2⁡t+1=sec2⁡ty25+1=x23x23−y25=1.
